[2025-08-19 01:19] fr1to : Cool, I think this is more useful than how some analytics websites calculate it for irl football!   There's a Pythagorean formula which is based on total GF - GA, and there's also a version that's based on total xGF - xA. There's statistical evidence that running up the score (xG) against bad teams is a sign of a good team, so the total versions are still useful, but it's better to go 2-0, 2-0 on xG than 4-0, 0-0 (for example).

[2025-10-31 12:53] shaun.frost : I'm fairly new around here and still learning too so I'm not the ideal person to give advice but I will say that one of my favorite feature in this game is the ability to retrain players to different positions.  If their skills are suitable for other positions and roles don't be afraid to experiment in giving them a shot there, e.g. defender with decent creative skills can easily be retrained to play in midfield, midfielder with high finishing to forward, central mid with good movement and crossing to winger or winger with poor crossing but good play making attributes to central midfielder, right winger to left winger, left back to right back/central defender etc. Not everyone learns it at same pace but it usually don't take more than 5 to 10 games untill they're natural in new role (depending on adaptability and other hidden attributes I think?)

[2026-06-20 17:12] furysk : My thoughts on the current system, and in general what i think is good or bad about it:  Good - It has brought the average age of a developing player down from what was basically 17-18 on the transfer list to 16-17.  That extra 30 days of development average for the people to utilize is very important imo in getting more mileage out of developing them, assuming their development age is close to their true age.    Good - the options available to train for lower level teams has expanded significantly.  Teams are less likely to settle on a few players in their school because of the age gap between school and the earliest available TL'd player (which takes a player exitting school or a team buying a guy out of school and TL'ing him at the earliest availability) and because of this more of the 'right guys' have a potential chance to be recruited in.  Bad - For higher level teams, this system is not nearly as helpful.  In some aspects, this design is a good thing, but they become reliant on finding a spot for lets say on average a 1M-1.5M at best prospect in their lineup card that would otherwise have a 10-12m player, meaning the cost of acquisition to them also has to include the potential value of losses incurred due to the fielding of that player, not just the amount they spent to bring them in.  Bad - it's a heavier overall investment cost now to find veteran players on the open market, because we're now dealing with not only lower understanding of veterans skills than when i first started but we are also dealing with a larger range of true valuation on the veteran players.  Bad - This system is reliant on human players not getting attached to a larger percentage of the players they develop, so that they are actually training players for sale value rather than trying to take them from league 4/tier 4 to the top.  I personally see too much wasted wage budget on middle aged guys that have stopped development because they reached the tier max that teams should have sold.
[2026-06-20 17:25] furysk : It is my personal opinion that potential solutions would be  School:  IMO - school should either be something that can be rotated still, or should be a place where we can send players we recruit from these pools.  If it were rotated, i think Derby you would either have to not send the rotated to the regional prospect pool, or you would have to set strict parameters so that only a small percentage (.5%-2%) of the players rotated out of the schools were released to the regional pools.  I think the schools should not be as local if this is the case, i think the clubs should be recruiting in potential youths from all over, so only 40-50% should be within the country.  The rest of the kids should want to go to the teams to be able to progress their careers, and here the big 5 regions are the best places to go.  That reduces the inflation of the big 5 regions pools some.  My idea for bringing guys in would be that if you don't like the primary guy from your school, then you can release them and have the school 'freed' for the guy you want to take a chance on.  They get paid the price you paid for them and the wage budget as if they are on the main club, and they have a limit to their development to where they can't sit in school for the entire 103 days of the contract, a team will eventually be losing develop time.  The player then can be brought up on their remaining deal.  Players that come to the school via yearly turnover do not cost a wage and must be signed on promotion still, so if teams don't want to utilize the school to develop they can cost cut.  These are just ideas i have, they can't both be implemented side by side they are simply ways to solve some of the issues created by the school setup as it sits now.
[2026-06-20 17:27] furysk : Heavier scouting investment cost - I think that veterans of the world should have a larger 'book' on them, and should have smaller ranges of skills and of potential values than players who are less experienced.  I would make barely experienced a wide range, somewhat slightly less wide ranged, fairly experienced even less range, and highly experienced should come with very little doubt as to what they can do.  Scouts should have plenty of communication with scouts between regions, and this should allow them to find more information on just basic phone conversations and tapes they can get for free.  Slowing down human players on building their teams is more frustrating than a good thing.

The data was published in the Journal of Sports Sciences and suggested that for every additional 10,000 people attending, home team advantage increased by 0.1 goals. Additionally, his study found that home teams are likely to be awarded more penalty kicks, and this is more likely with inexperienced referees.[5]*  *An evolutionary psychology explanation for the home advantage effect refers to observed behavioral and physiological responses in animals when they are defending their home territory against intruders. This causes a rise in aggression and testosterone levels in the defenders. A similar effect has been observed in football with testosterone levels being significantly higher in home games than in away games. Goalkeepers, the last line of defense, have particularly strong testosterone changes when playing against a bitter rival as compared to a training season.*

[2025-01-01 21:02] derbymanager : So, to remove any confusion, there are several things at play here:  - Every position has certain popularity assigned. It works in such way that 12th in d2 is more popular than 1st in d3 (and similarly for other divisions). However, your team doesn't automatically get the popularity for its position. Instead, every Monday the popularity moves a certain percentage towards the popularity for that position. E.g. if popularity for your position is 12 but you are at 8, on Monday it will jump to 8.6 or whatever, I don't know exactly. So, it's unlikely your popularity drops with promotion (it could happen if your team went quickly down and then back up by a big margin or some similar edge case).  - After this popularity is calculated, all teams are sorted in order from most popular to least popular and a tier is assigned to them so that there are 20 teams in top tier, 50 in the next one etc... Same is done for players, best 200 players are top tier, next 1000 are next tier etc... This is what actually affects who are you able to buy. So, depending on which teams go up or down in popularity your tier can change even if your popularity stays the same. E.g. if your popularity is 8.6 and 10 teams with popularity 8.7 go down below 8.6, you would overtake them when it comes to team tier. This shouldn't make too much of a difference though since some other teams will overtake you and you'll always be pretty close to where you should be.  - Finally, there are also end of season bonuses in popularity for final standing as well as for cup(s) if you progressed a bit so going up a division will almost certainly improve your popularity/tier. As I said, I can imagine an edge case where that's not the case, but it vast majority of cases it should improve.
[2025-01-01 21:07] derbymanager : As for finances, well, higher division improves broadcasting revenue (which affects the salary cap) like so: 200k, 300k, 500k, 1M. That alone makes a huge difference, but with higher tier you also get better sponsors, stadium revenue etc... So financially I can't imagine this not being an improvement. Even match win bonus increases by 100k, although you might win less so you might earn less than before. In d4 20 wins would net you 2M, while in d3 you only need 10 wins to get those same 2M...

Abstracting away the buildup has been controversial, but I don't think the game is worse off.   4. Transfer windows - I was a big advocate of adding them because I hated how a given percentage of the contract is always wasted due to renewals happening before expiry. However, given how dynamic the game is and how often things change - being able to transfer players in and out is essential. Example - Alin knowing he'll be relegating a couple of weeks in advance has been spending his time to prepare adequately for next season. This would have been impossible if we had the transfer windows. Another example is how you play the game - you've made so many changes at Munster - now imagine joining and waiting a whole month before being allowed to tinker with the squad. I think down the line, having this flexibility of instant impact via the market is key and it's overall a positive.  5. Contracts ending end of the season ties up with the previous point, so won't be repeating myself.  6. I actually agree here - I've even been advocating for more player filled divisions and even adding timespan to the game, e.g. - we all play 3 seasons and then the game starts all over again and this is how we accumulate score. I also said to Derby that the first season of the game where there was not a single bot team in D4 was amazing. Chaotic, but amazing. Then again - there's a charm in being able to fight off the odds and win D1 against bots that were created as unbeatable. No one has done it yet, but it makes the chase even more tempting. So yeah - I think this one has tradeoffs, but I think both approaches are equally interesting/rewarding.  7. On mentors - I also kind of agree here - I don't really like how they work, I want them to exist, but I also have doubts about how they're currently being implemented. That being said - I know why Derby does things this way and I agree it's the right direction. The execution is not perfect, but I'm sure over time we'll find a way to make them feel less unpredictable.  8. On player graphs visible by default - I think this is a byproduct of the game not providing enough data. Also kind of agree as you don't really have proper training facilities, because everyone maxes out 1 of the 3 just so they can get max possible intensity from one of the areas. Splitting mentors over all 4 is stupid as well as we keep limiting our personal training to "Technical" only. And let's face it - everyone maxes out Technical because Finishing and Handling are the most important skills in the game. So yes - having training unified was more intuitive and allowed more freedom.  Overall, I think you are bringing valid points - there are issues in the game, but the game itself relies on players like you providing feedback. You've been with us for a long time and know how the game works (and how it worked), so it will definitely be a loss if you decide to stop playing (which I hope you won't).

[2025-08-06 11:07] laura060131 : Btw, what does the bar below pitch in match screen represents?
[2025-08-06 11:16] poletz : Added the bar below the field on end-match screen that shows relative power between the two teams after modifiers (it's complicated).  * it's complicated because power doesn't go from 1 to 10, and even if it did, a power of 2 shouldn't mean 2x the power of 1. Instead, weak players will have power of around 8 and great players of around 16. But averages of the whole teams bring the numbers closer together, and when they're in the same division the difference is even smaller. So while a team with average power of 12 vs team with average power of 13 is a huge difference, the bar would show 48% vs 52%. I made it so that the bar shows the difference in average power by a certain fixed amount (every 1% on the bar is X) so that 12 vs 13 looks exactly the same as 10 vs 9 or any other numbers that are 1 apart... Basically, the bars don't represent power but the difference in power and is another arbitrary stat to help you analyse your games...

[2025-11-11 08:44] derbymanager : I uderstand that sponsors downgrading are extra harsh on the budget but I feel micro-managing the facilities to that level kills verisimilitude. Even choosing what to upgrade is against my wishes but I can at least believe that manager can have some impact on the board in that regard... But when facilities downgrade they simply downgrade all around. There isn't enough money for the stadium and the chairs have gone old, some are missing, the gym floor gets ruined, billboards fall apart etc... We don't have an option to partially downgrade everything so, instead, something is chosen at random. We as managers have to do what we can to avoid getting there.  But since you can always upgrade, you can get that sponsorship star back. You just have to sell a player. Now, before you jump that it's unfair, you would have to sell a player either way. For example, sedan is earning more than 300k per day + match revenue. And the missing money for facilities is also exactly 300k. So, the board could have kept facilities at 100% but that would mean the team has no money to renew contracts (on which they've spent almost 9M this season). Considering that the players in and out are basically the same, that the current budget is 9M, and that the team started with around 9M, it's almost as if all the money from facilities went into contract extensions. Which is what the board aims for, keep the players, the rest will come with results. So, if the board had invested 100% into facilities Sedan would now be without money and would have to sell someone to extend the next contract.  For Ipswich it's similar although the numbers don't fit as nicely. The board keeps the revenues at 150k per day + match revenue. Spending on extensions and 1 new player is about 21M, and revenue from sales about 18M, allowing the team to get from -3M to about 0 now. If the board invested 100%, the team would be losing 300k per day to keep the facilities up and would have to sell players...
